summary: Independent review of the stale flip-owner lockout fix at the session roll. THE DEFECT IS LIVE-CONFIRMED, not theoretical: on 2026-09-11 at 05:21 ET DBGI was still looping [V2-FLIP-OWNER-RECOVERY] evaluated=9660 recovered=3220 pending=6440 entry_allowed=0 reason=insufficient_unambiguous_evidence open=0 filled_accounts=1 position_ids=0 age_ms=32646616, i.e. 6,440 warnings and an unresolvable state, because the recovery requires BOTH fill accounts AND position_ids and DBGI had filled_accounts=1 with position_ids=0. ⛔ MY OWN EARLIER DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND CODEX-2 CORRECTED IT: I told the operator the 04:00 roll had never run because no bar arrived. It DID run; its live-bar guard blocked owner retirement while still advancing the session anchor, so no later bar would retry the cleanup. That is why the state was permanent rather than merely delayed, and codex's mechanism is the one recorded here. THE FIX: _apply_session_anchor_reset gains owner_boundary_is_current, defaulting to the original _fanout_identity_bar_is_live check; the CLOCK-DRIVEN sweep passes True because the sweep is itself the current-session boundary proof, while the bar-driven caller passes the live-bar check explicitly. Retirement is still gated on fresh position evidence and on having no open positions — those branches are unchanged context lines, so nothing was loosened; only the live-bar precondition, which a silent symbol can never satisfy and which was the bug, is removed for the clock path. Both new controls are behavioural and one is DISCRIMINATING: test_time_roll_retires_a_flat_unknown_owner_without_waiting_for_a_live_bar asserts rolled==['DBGI'], phase idle, opportunity_id 0, fill accounts cleared, and identity+owner writes both (False,'session_reset_flat'); test_historical_bar_reset_cannot_retire_current_durable_ownership asserts the OPPOSITE direction — a historical bar reset must NOT retire, phase stays unknown, opportunity_id 123, and identity_writes==[] and owner_writes==[]. Mutations against test_schwab_1m_v2_session_time_roll.py + test_v2_flip_owned_first_entry.py + test_v2_flip_entry_ownership_store.py (66 passed baseline): reinstating the bug by passing owner_boundary_is_current=False on the sweep -> 1 failed RED; hardcoding True on the BAR path -> 1 failed RED. Both directions are pinned. ⚠ THREE MUTANTS SURVIVED AND I AM RECORDING THEM RATHER THAN OMITTING THEM. (a) The None default branch is dead for the two real callers, which both pass explicitly — harmless, untested by construction. (b) and (c) Dropping the _flip_owner_evidence_fresh gate and dropping the flip_owner_open_positions gate both leave the focused suite green. ⛔ BOTH ARE PRE-EXISTING: they are unchanged CONTEXT lines in this diff, not code #948 introduces, and this PR does not weaken them — so they do not block this pin. BUT #948 deliberately widens the population that reaches those gates to include silent symbols that never receive a bar, which raises the stakes on two safety branches that nothing currently exercises. Boarded as a separate follow-up item; a control asserting that a stale-evidence owner and an owner with open positions are each NOT retired by the clock sweep would close it. Controlled full unit pair: base a93fe95 is TREE-IDENTICAL to af31b02 which I had already measured (git diff empty), so the baseline applies directly — base 46 failed/3603 passed, head 46 failed/3605 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed compared as sorted sets. Ruff clean on src+tests. Ancestor test PASS. One commit, one recognised agent marker, authored by codex, reviewer differs. ⛔ DEPLOY NOTE, OPERATOR-DECIDED: the operator has chosen to deploy BEFORE today's 07:00 ET entry window rather than wait for the after-close window, because the live mitigation was a V2-only restart and any further restart would reinstate the lockout. I raised the timing concern and he reaffirmed. The restart must still run the full checklist: both accounts flat, bar-gap continuity, process-env flags re-verified after the restart, and boot-hold released before 07:00.
